newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Minister sees Svyazinvest stake to consortium.
newsitem.headline: Minister sees Svyazinvest stake to consortium.

text.p: The winner of the sale of 25 percent plus one share in Russian telecom holding company Svyazinvest is likely to be a consortium of Russian and foreign companies, privatisation minister Alfred Kokh told Ekho-Moskvy radio on Wednesday, Ekho Moskvy said in a statement.

"In the opinion of Kokh, the buyer of the Svyazinvest shares will be a consortium, which will include Russian and foreign investors," the statement said. It also said he thought a price of $1.38 billion for the stake, which has a $1.18 billion starting price, was "realistic".

Kokh, Deputy Prime Minister who as head of the State Property Committee is in charge of privatisation, also said a further 24 percent stake in the company would be privatised next year, repeating statements he made earlier this month.

AO Svyazinvest has controlling stakes in 85 regional Russian telecoms and long distance carrier Rostelekom, but officials have different opinions as to whether Svyazinvest needs a strategic partner to help guide the company.
Analysts say Svyazinvest is a key to the domestic telecoms industry. The 25-plus-one stake is large enough to block changes to the charter of the company.
